chapter: Moving to California and the war years
title: Leading the Teddy Bunn Group; Leonard Feather
summary: During the war years he had his own group, and Leonard Feather looked him up for pickup record dates.

blocks.x: Who all, then -- you started to work with other organizations, then, right? Like during the war years, after you didn't get inducted.
Well, I'm asking you. You didn't get inducted. You went down to the Army and they didn't take you.
That would have been around '42, right?
Then is that when you started playing with Louis Jordan?
No? Who did you play with, then, around --
What was it -- just under your own name?
Uh-huh. What about those records that you made with Leonard Feather and Leo that were so --
Oh, that was just a pickup.
He came in town and he heard about me, you know, from overseas.
I think Leonard Feather lives out here.
Yeah. Lives out this way. Yeah, I knew
Yeah, he's still around. He's still writing a column, I think.
The L.A. Times. He must be pretty old now.
Well, He is. Because if he knew me when I was over there in Europe, you know, and he'd been collecting my records by that time, you know he's old.
I think the man is about 55.
